To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) computer games can be used as a source of pixel-accurate ground truth, and that (ii) this approach enables training models that are more accurate than state-of-the-art models trained on real-world data alone.

(1) it is possible to rapidly create pixel-level semantic annotations of synthetic images by leveraging the game’s internal communication; (2) the created annotations are of high quality; and (3) using the created annotations significantly increases the accuracy of semantic segmentation models.
